amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **And a rectum the ASV renders indefinitely is not an anarthrous one.** Where the article morpheme stands on the rectum, the ASV writes an indefinite article before the rectum's own word, and the phrase's single *the* stands before the construct — `נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם` → *the body of a man* — nothing is fronted: the *a* is that noun's own under rule 15, one word is not determined twice, and the article is `unrepresented` under this rule's last sentence while the construct takes a supplied *the*. What forces fronting is a rectum the ASV leaves with no determiner at all, as `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone* is, so read which determiner stands before the rectum's word before counting the phrase's *the*s. **A construct relation the ASV recasts as an English possessive is not a fronting either.** Where the ASV writes the rectum as a possessive standing before its head noun — `מִלַּת מַלְכָּא` → *the king's matter*, `שַׁלִּיטָא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the king's captain*, `שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ` → *the king's gate* — the *the* at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's own word, because an English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor and not of the head noun. So the article on the rectum takes it and the construct noun keeps only its own word, a present article morpheme taking its English before a supplied one does; supply a *the* on the construct only where the ASV writes a second one, as `רַב טַבָּחַיָּא דִּי מַלְכָּא` → *the captain of the king's guard* does. Do not read the left edge as evidence of fronting: what fronting answers to is an anarthrous rectum, and here the rectum is the very word the *the* determines. **Read that as the determiner of the possessive, not as the word *the*, and read it whether or not the possessor carries an article of its own.** An English possessive expression takes the determiner of the possessor whatever that determiner is, so an indefinite *a* standing at the phrase's left edge stands before the possessor's word exactly as a *the* does, and where the possessor's word carries no article morpheme the determiner the ASV supplies still goes to that word rather than to the construct noun: `נְשִׂיא בֵית־אָב` → *a prince of* ***a fathers*** *house* gives *a fathers* to `אָב` and *of ... house* to `בַּיִת`, discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25. This is rule 15's supplied determiner placed by this rule's own reasoning — the noun that licenses an English *a* in such a phrase is the possessor, since *a father's house* is the house of *a* father — and the construct noun takes a determiner of its own only where the ASV writes a second one, on the terms just given. A `דִּי` or other relational morpheme standing between the two nouns is rendered inside the possessive and shares the rectum's unit under rule 30. **And a chain the ASV renders attributively under rule 28 places its supplied determiner on these same terms.** Where the ASV writes the construct noun as an attributive standing before the rectum's own word — `קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו` → *the tall cedars thereof*, `מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו` → *the choice fir trees thereof*, `יְרַק דֶּשֶׁא` → *the green herb*, `בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן` → *The virgin daughter of Zion* — and no article morpheme stands in the phrase, the single written *the* stands before the construct noun's word and that noun takes it as a supplied one, exactly as it does where the same chain is written with *of*. Do not hand it to the rectum on the ground that the rectum is the head noun of the English phrase: rule 15's direction to read the noun of the expression rather than its leftmost word governs a numeral and the noun it counts, where the numeral is not a noun the ASV determines at all, and it does not reach a construct chain, whose determiners this rule counts. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as above: where the ASV writes one for each, each noun takes the one standing before its own word, and where an article morpheme stands on the rectum the fronting sentences above govern as before. The unit still heads on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31, so `קוֹמַת` → *the tall* heads on *tall*. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: 2KI.19.23 writes two structurally identical attributively-rendered construct chains side by side, each with one supplied the and no article morpheme in the phrase, and the verse pass placed the determiner on opposite members: קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו -> the tall cedars thereof on the rectum, citing rule 15's noun-of-the-expression sentence, and מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו -> the choice fir trees thereof on the construct, citing rule 29. Rule 29 had no sentence about a chain rule 28 renders attributively, so nothing in the contract told a reader which of the two rules governs, and rule 15's numeral sentence was read across a construct chain it excludes in its own terms. The added paragraph states the answer rule 29's existing permission already implies (supply a the on a construct noun where no article morpheme is present) and marks the boundary against rule 15, so the case is decided rather than argued again. It contradicts no corpus line: rule 29's own examples all put a supplied the on the construct, and the chapter's three other attributive chains (19.21 בְּתוּלַת -> The virgin, 19.26 יְרַק -> as the green, and מִבְחוֹר) do the same. Nothing else in rule 29 is changed; the fronting, indefinite-rectum, possessive, proper-name and transliterated-article paragraphs and the closing unrepresented sentence are quoted back whole.

conventions: Where a construct chain is rendered attributively under rule 28 and the ASV writes one the for the phrase with no article morpheme standing in it, that the goes to the construct noun, whose own English word it stands before, and the rectum keeps only its own word: קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו -> the tall cedars thereof, מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו -> the choice fir trees thereof (19.23), יְרַק דֶּשֶׁא -> as the green herb (19.26), בְּתוּלַת בַּת־צִיּוֹן -> The virgin daughter of Zion (19.21). Rule 15's direction to read the noun of the expression rather than its leftmost word governs a numeral and the noun it counts and does not reach a chain, whose determiners rule 29 counts. 19.23's first chain was corrected in reconciliation; do not read the rectum's position as the English head noun as grounds to move the determiner back.

הַמֶּלֶךְ חִזְקִיָּהוּ is read by the the the ASV writes and not by the phrase it stands in. At 19.1 the ASV writes king Hezekiah with no the and the article is unrepresented under rule 29's last sentence; at 19.5, inside עַבְדֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ חִזְקִיָּהוּ -> the servants of king Hezekiah, the rectum is rendered anarthrously and the phrase's single the is fronted to the left edge, so the article takes it and the construct עַבְדֵי stays bare. The two verses are not a split, and a supplied the on the construct is permitted only where no article morpheme is present.

לְבַדְּךָ is counted verse by verse against the pronouns the ASV writes. At 19.15 -> thou art the God even thou alone, two thou's answer to two morphemes: the explicit אַתָּה takes the first and the suffix the second, while לְ + בַד fuse into alone. At 19.19 -> thou Jehovah art God alone, the one thou is the explicit אַתָּה's, nothing is left for the suffix, and it is unrepresented; rule 30 excludes a suffix on the construct noun from the fusion. BSB represents that suffix, which is the documented difference.

A serial auxiliary verb the ASV renders adverbially takes the adverb, and the verb it governs keeps its own English: שׁוּב at 19.9 (וַיָּשָׁב וַיִּשְׁלַח מַלְאָכִים -> he sent messengers again) and יָסַף at 19.30 (וְיָסְפָה ... שֹׁרֶשׁ -> shall again take root) each take again, with the auxiliary carrying the finite frame at 19.30. Do not fold such an again into the following verb as a phrasal particle under rule 44, and do not mark it added: the auxiliary verb is the morpheme it renders. At 19.9 the ASV writes no connective for either waw of that clause, and both are unrepresented under rule 14.

report: One real cross-verse split, and it sits inside a single verse. 2KI.19.23 writes two structurally identical attributively-rendered construct chains side by side and places their supplied `the` on opposite members: קוֹמַת אֲרָזָיו -> *the tall cedars thereof* gave it to the rectum under rule 15, while מִבְחוֹר בְּרֹשָׁיו -> *the choice fir trees thereof* gave it to the construct under rule 29. No article morpheme stands in either phrase and nothing in the source licenses the difference.

Patched 19.23 so both give it to the construct noun. That is what rule 29 licenses directly (supply a the on a construct noun where no article morpheme is present) and what the chapter's three other attributive chains already do: 19.21 בְּתוּלַת -> *The virgin*, 19.26 יְרַק -> *as the green*, and מִבְחוֹר itself. The accepted קוֹמַת unit was the lone outlier, three to one.

Cleared as licensed rather than split: the relative-plus-resumptive family (19.4 fused *whom*; 19.16 *wherewith* + *him*; 19.10 and 19.28 *in*/*by* + relative with the suffix unrepresented; 19.33 all three rendered) runs the same count of English words against present morphemes in every verse. לְבַדְּךָ at 19.15 (*thou alone*, suffix takes *thou*) and 19.19 (bare *alone*, suffix unrepresented) is that count run on two different ASV renderings. הַמֶּלֶךְ חִזְקִיָּהוּ at 19.1 (no *the* written, article unrepresented) and 19.5 (one *the* written and the rectum anarthrous, so rule 29's fronting) differs only by what the ASV wrote.

The eleven `added` units, which the candidate table is blind to, were read end to end against the folded-in cases and agree. Supplied object pronouns (19.1, 19.20) are added while written suffixes take theirs (19.11, 19.32, 19.34). Supplied possessives (19.4, 19.21, 19.22) are added while suffixes take theirs. Supplied coordinators (19.21, 19.23) are added where the Hebrew juxtaposes, while a present waw takes *And when* (19.9, 19.35), *that* (19.19, 19.25), *So*, *Then*, *therefore*, *wherefore*, *For* and *But* elsewhere. Supplied subordinators (19.25 *how*, 19.37 *as*) are added where no conjunction stands in the clause, while כְּ takes *when* at 19.1. The two *even*s divide correctly: 19.15's goes to the written הוּא, 19.22's is added because the clause's one marker stands on מִי and עַל is not an extent preposition.

Every BSB disagreement in the report is a documented convention difference, not an error: object markers (rule 16), paragogic nun (rule 32), the לְ of לֵאמֹר (rule 27), articles where the ASV writes no the (rule 29), prepositions the recasting silences (rules 40, 21), resumptive suffixes the ASV renders once (rule 22), and the lexicalized אֲדֹנָי suffix (rule 57). The fifteen Td cases are the single largest group and are exactly the convention rule 29's last sentence states.

Four conventions recorded and one amendment returned. The amendment closes the gap the patch exposed: rule 29 never said where a supplied determiner goes when rule 28 renders the chain attributively, which is what let rule 15's numeral sentence be read across a construct chain.
